title: An open Add-Shift sheet's stale in-memory draft can silently overwrite a same-day edit just pulled from another device
where: AddShiftSheet's list/events/note state is captured once at mount from props (index.html:4076, 4083-4084) and never resynced; saveDayShifts unconditionally overwrites shifts[dateKey]/dayEvents[dateKey]/notes[dateKey] with that draft (index.html:2857-2874); the cross-device poll can apply a newer remote blob into the same state at any time the sheet is open (applyData at 2317/2325-2326 via the 15s interval, focus, and visibilitychange refetch at index.html:2547-2574)
detail: AddShiftSheet is only mounted/unmounted on `sheetDate` null↔value transitions (index.html:3613-3618: `{sheetDate && <AddShiftSheet .../>}`, no `key` prop keying it to the date), so while it stays open its `list`/`events`/`note` state — seeded once from `existing`/`existingEvents`/`existingNote` at mount — never re-reads the `shifts`/`dayEvents`/`notes` props even if they change underneath it. But those props DO change underneath it: the cross-device refetch (2547-2574) fires on the 15s interval and immediately on `focus`/visible-`visibilitychange`, and on a content difference calls `applyData(row.data,{keepPeriod:true})`, which does a plain `setShifts(d.shifts)`/`setDayEvents(d.dayEvents)`/`setNotes(d.notes)` (2317, 2325-2326) — a full replace, not a per-day merge. When the sheet is later saved or dismissed-with-dirty-state, `saveDayShifts` (2857-2858) does `n[dateKey]=arr` (or the dayEvents/notes equivalents at 2867/2873) against whatever `prev` currently is, but `arr`/`events`/`note` are still the sheet's original stale draft.
failure: Nurse signs into the same account on two devices. On device A she opens the Add-Shift sheet for a day and gets interrupted — she switches apps/tabs (backgrounding triggers no refetch, but returning fires an immediate `visibilitychange`/`focus` refetch). Meanwhile on device B she (or someone else with the login) added a shift to that same day; that write is now the newer cloud row. When she returns to device A, the refetch pulls device B's shift for that day into `shifts` — but the still-open sheet's `list` doesn't include it. She finishes her edit on device A and hits Save: `saveDayShifts` writes only her stale `list` for that date, so device B's just-synced shift for that day is silently discarded, then propagated to the cloud 500ms later with no conflict warning.
fix: When shifts/dayEvents/notes for the currently-open `dateKey` change while the sheet is mounted, either re-seed the sheet's local draft (e.g. a useEffect keyed on the incoming day's content that merges or warns instead of overwriting) or have the cross-device refetch skip applying changes to a day that has an open, dirty sheet and re-check once it closes.
